title: run.skill.md Phase 9 QA gate failure emits post-tag harness files creating untagged commit
description: When qa_passed is false, Phase 9 writes a suppression signal catalogue entry and updates index.md and the run file's emittedSignals array. These writes happen after Phase 7 (Commit) and Phase 8 (Tag) have already executed, so git_commit must be called a second time to capture them. The result is two commits with identical messages and the run tag pointing to the first commit, which lacks the suppression signal and the final run file state. Run traceability is degraded: the canonical tag does not cover all harness artifacts produced by the run.
proposed_resolution:
Restructure the commit/tag phases around `git commit --amend` and hash-targeted tagging:

**QA fail path**: After Phase 9 writes the suppression signal and updates the run file, call `git commit --amend` (no new message) to fold those writes into the Phase 7 execution commit. There is then one canonical commit. Call `tag_run` pointing at HEAD (the amended commit) as normal. No candidate tag is created.

**QA pass path**: Phase 7 (Commit) produces the execution commit; record its hash. Phase 9 calls `bump_version` (creates a version bump commit on top) and `create_candidate_tag`. Then call `tag_run` with the Phase 7 execution commit hash — not HEAD — so the run tag lands on the implementation commit rather than the version bump commit.

This requires: (1) `git_commit` to expose an `--amend` mode or the skill to call Bash for `git commit --amend --no-edit --no-gpg-sign`; (2) `tag_run` to accept an optional `commit_hash` parameter so it can tag a historic commit via `git tag <name> <hash>`. Phase 8 (Tag) should be merged into Phase 9 so tagging always happens once after all writes complete.
